behavior: gh is authenticated on ace2 and works from a NON-interactive shell, not only a login shell (the f4 lesson from ANSIBLE-028: shell class matters)
verification: ssh -o ForwardAgent=no ace2 'gh auth status' && ssh -o ForwardAgent=no ace2 'gh api /user --jq .login'

behavior: An agent inside a tmux session clones a PRIVATE repo, commits, pushes a branch and opens a PR with no human and no agent forwarding; the test artefacts are cleaned up afterwards
verification: scp specs/ANSIBLE-033-dev-node-credentials/probes/f2-private-repo-flow.sh ace2:/tmp/ansible-033-f2.sh && ssh -o ForwardAgent=no ace2 'tmux kill-session -t ansible033f2 2>/dev/null; tmux new-session -d -s ansible033f2 "bash /tmp/ansible-033-f2.sh"' && for i in $(seq 1 60); do ssh -o ForwardAgent=no ace2 'test -f /tmp/ansible-033-f2.result' && break; sleep 5; done && ssh -o ForwardAgent=no ace2 'grep -qx F2_OK /tmp/ansible-033-f2.result'
evidence: NOTE at authoring time: the probe body lives in probes/f2-private-repo-flow.sh rather than inline. Inline it would need three quoting layers (ssh -> tmux -> bash) and would expand $WORK on the controller instead of the node — the same class of defect as ANSIBLE-028's f4, whose criterion text turned out to be unrunnable as written. The fixture is mlorentedev/kubelab-devnode-fixture: PRIVATE (the earliest draft cloned mlorentedev/kubelab, which is public, so it could have passed without ever proving private access), README-only, and purpose-built so an acceptance branch cannot collide with real work. The probe asserts the fixture is private, clones over an explicit HTTPS URL, and asserts origin is HTTPS — otherwise a configured git protocol could route the push over SSH and test a forwarded key instead of the PAT. STANDING ASSUMPTION: the fixture must stay visible to the DEV-NODE TOKEN, not merely to the operator — it was chosen while the operator's own gh could see it. If repository access is ever narrowed (AC7 invites exactly that at rotation) or the repo is transferred, this probe dies at the clone with a generic auth error that is easy to misread as a broken credential. Re-check the fixture whenever repository access changes. BLOCKED 2026-08-08 — FIXTURE UNRESOLVED: the first attempt used mlorentedev/go-dsa-sample, which is ARCHIVED and therefore read-only; the push returned 403 'This repository was archived', which reads like a permissions failure. It is not one. Everything before the push succeeded on ace2: `gh api repos/... --jq .private` returned true and `git clone` over HTTPS completed, so the PAT demonstrably reaches private repositories — only the write half is unproven. The probe now checks `.archived` up front and reports F2_FIXTURE_ARCHIVED so this cannot be mistaken for a credential fault again. Choosing the replacement needs a human: every private non-archived repo of this owner is ACTIVELY used (resume, knowledge, fae-brain, openkm-brain, biwenger-mvp — all pushed 2026-08-07/08), and `knowledge` is the Obsidian vault with an auto-committer, so pointing a PR-creating probe at any of them risks colliding with real work. Options for the operator: unarchive a dormant repo for the duration, or create a dedicated throwaway private fixture (the token cannot create one itself — no `administration` permission, which is itself a small confirmation that the permission scoping holds). RESOLVED 2026-08-08 — the operator chose a dedicated fixture, mlorentedev/kubelab-devnode-fixture, created under the operator's own credential. Fixing the fixture then exposed a SECOND defect the 403 had been masking: `gh pr create` aborted with 'you must first push the current branch to a remote' straight after a push that returned 0, because `clone --depth 1` implies `--single-branch` and the pinned fetch refspec cannot create refs/remotes/origin/<branch>, so `@{upstream}` does not resolve. The probe now passes --head explicitly. With both fixed, the full f2 body runs green end to end (F2_OK, exit 0, trap leaving no branch and no PR) — but that run was executed FROM THE WORKSTATION under the OPERATOR's token, so it evidences the flow only. It is not AC2: AC2 requires this same script on ace2, inside tmux, under the dev-node PAT. PASS 2026-08-08 — that node-side run has now happened, verbatim, returning F2_OK and exit 0, with f1 re-run first as a post-reboot precondition and cleanup confirmed independently of the probe's own verdict (fixture left at main with zero open PRs, no tmux server on the node). It also settled the standing scope question above: the fixture was created AFTER the token was minted, and the clone succeeded, so All-repositories does pre-authorise later-created repositories. The flow is now exonerated at every step, so a node-side failure localises cleanly: at step 1 or 2 (the `.private` check or the clone) the repository-access axis is at fault, NOT `contents:write`; at step 4 the token/API axis is. Step 1/2 is a live possibility rather than a formality — the fixture was created 2026-08-08, AFTER the PAT was minted, so the node-side clone is the first empirical test of the runbook's claim that All-repositories scope pre-authorises repositories created after minting.

behavior: The token is fine-grained (not classic) and its refused permissions are actually refused — a push touching .github/workflows/ is rejected by GitHub, and rejected for that reason rather than incidentally
verification: scp specs/ANSIBLE-033-dev-node-credentials/probes/f3-workflow-refusal.sh ace2:/tmp/ansible-033-f3.sh && ssh -o ForwardAgent=no ace2 'tmux kill-session -t ansible033f3 2>/dev/null; tmux new-session -d -s ansible033f3 "bash /tmp/ansible-033-f3.sh"' && for i in $(seq 1 60); do ssh -o ForwardAgent=no ace2 'test -f /tmp/ansible-033-f3.result' && break; sleep 5; done && ssh -o ForwardAgent=no ace2 'grep -qx F3_OK /tmp/ansible-033-f3.result'
evidence: NOTE at authoring time: the `github_pat_` prefix distinguishes fine-grained from classic (`ghp_`) and IS executable, as is the workflow-write refusal — the probe pushes a file under .github/workflows/ and requires GitHub to reject it, distinguishing F3_OK (rejected naming the workflow scope) from F3_WRONG_REASON (rejected by a network or auth fault, which proves nothing). The 90-day expiry and the All-repositories scope are NOT machine-readable from the API for fine-grained PATs — they are confirmed by inspecting the token's settings page, and that manual step is part of this criterion rather than pretended to be automated. Do not mark this feature verified on the executable half alone.

behavior: The credential is delivered reproducibly by the dev_node role from SOPS common, and provisioning converges: a second pass reports changed=0 with no task flipping to changed
verification: bash -o pipefail -c "make provision NODE=ace2 ENV=staging TAGS=dev_node | tee /tmp/ansible-033-c1" && bash -o pipefail -c "make provision NODE=ace2 ENV=staging TAGS=dev_node | tee /tmp/ansible-033-c2" && grep -qE 'changed=0 .*failed=0' /tmp/ansible-033-c2 && ! grep -A1 'Read the token gh currently holds' /tmp/ansible-033-c2 | grep -q skipping
evidence: NOTE at authoring time: each pass runs under `bash -o pipefail` because `make ... | tee` otherwise reports tee's exit status, so a FAILED first pass would be silently ignored and only the second recap checked. TAGS=, not --tags: make rejects --tags (the ANSIBLE-028 f2 lesson). The aggregate `changed=0` is necessary but not sufficient — tasks.md requires reading the per-task list of the second pass, not just the recap line. STRENGTHENED 2026-08-08 after this command PASSED while the credential was never delivered: convergence alone cannot distinguish 'converged with the token in place' from 'converged because every identity task was skipped'. AC4 claims DELIVERY, so the probe now also asserts that the role saw a non-empty token. It keys on 'Read the token gh currently holds' rather than the login task, because that read is guarded ONLY by the token being non-empty — on an already-converged node the login task legitimately skips, so asserting on the login task would fail against a correctly-provisioned host. Root cause of the original false green: the playbook's SOPS-decryption pre_tasks were untagged, so a TAGS= run skipped them and every SOPS-sourced role var silently fell back to its default.

behavior: No prod credential is reachable from ace2. The age-key absence is the load-bearing part: per SEC-SOPS-001 (#889) any age key on this node would decrypt prod, so this criterion guards the assumption the whole spec rests on
verification: ssh -o ForwardAgent=no ace2 '! test -e ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt && ! test -e ~/.age/key.txt && ! test -e /etc/sops/age.key && ! command -v sops >/dev/null && ! grep -rqi prod ~/.kube/ 2>/dev/null'
evidence: NOTE at authoring time: the kubeconfig half greps the CONTENTS of ~/.kube/ rather than matching filenames. A prod context can sit inside ~/.kube/config while no ~/.kube/*prod* file exists, so the filename-only check in the first draft would have passed with prod cluster access present. The check deliberately does NOT assert ~/.kube is absent: AC5 claims no *prod* credential, and ADR-058 D2's dev loop may legitimately add a staging kubeconfig later. grep on a missing directory exits 2, so the negation still holds on a node with no ~/.kube at all.

behavior: The token never lands in a process argument, a log line, or a world-readable file; gh owns it in its own credential store
verification: grep -A8 'gh auth login' infra/ansible/roles/dev_node/tasks/main.yml | grep -q 'no_log: true' && ! grep -qE -- '--with-token[^|]*dev_node_github_token' infra/ansible/roles/dev_node/tasks/main.yml && ssh -o ForwardAgent=no ace2 'test "$(stat -c %a ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml)" = 600'
evidence: NOTE at authoring time: the no_log check is scoped to the 8 lines following the `gh auth login` task, because a bare file-wide grep passes whenever ANY task in the role carries no_log — including one unrelated to the credential. The permission check targets gh's actual secret sink (~/.config/gh/hosts.yml) and asserts mode 600 exactly; the first draft compared the containing directory with `-le 700`, which is a numeric comparison on an octal string and would accept 0644.

behavior: Expiry day is a scheduled event, not a mystery outage: a rotation runbook exists naming the failure symptom, the mint/re-provision/revoke sequence, and a prompt to reconsider the repository scope
verification: test -f docs/runbooks/dev-node-token-rotation.md && grep -qi '401' docs/runbooks/dev-node-token-rotation.md && grep -qi 'revoke' docs/runbooks/dev-node-token-rotation.md && grep -qi 'repository access' docs/runbooks/dev-node-token-rotation.md && grep -qi 'mint' docs/runbooks/dev-node-token-rotation.md && grep -q 'make provision NODE=ace2' docs/runbooks/dev-node-token-rotation.md
evidence: NOTE at authoring time: keyword greps cannot prove a runbook is operational, only that it is not empty. The list is therefore anchored on the things whose ABSENCE would make rotation fail in practice — the symptom (401), the re-provision command as it must actually be typed, and the revoke step that is easiest to forget once the replacement works.
